first_impression.reaction: Googled 'bali wedding venues' on the train. First line splits Bali into four areas, which is exactly how I'd want to start. Jump links and a table up top, nice on a phone. The table is wide though, and I still have no idea what any of these cost. Lots of 'Not published'. Bookmarked for the capacity table, probably won't enquire.

journey.quote: Bali wedding venues fall into four areas: the clifftops of the Bukit and Uluwatu, the beaches of Nusa Dua and Jimbaran, the west coast at Seminyak, and the river valleys around Ubud.
journey.reaction: Answer in the first sentence. I now know how to think about Bali. Good.

journey.quote: Published capacities range from a 16-guest hidden room in Seminyak to garden and ballroom spaces for several hundred in Nusa Dua and at AYANA, so match the space to your numbers before you fall for the view.
journey.reaction: Useful and specific. A 16-guest hidden room sounds fun.
Thank you. I can skip straight to Uluwatu.

journey.section: Bali wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: | Venue | Area | Setting | Ceremony | Exclusive use |
journey.reaction: Five columns on a phone means sideways scrolling. And the exclusive use column is 'Not published' for almost everyone, so it's a wasted column for me. Where's a price or capacity column?

journey.quote: Ceremony options:** Outdoors, Champa Garden, SKY, the AYANA Villa, KISIK Pier, the Asmara Gazebo from the Javanese royal palace and Bale Kencana, with its stone paths and Balinese split gate.
journey.reaction: Long list of names I don't know yet. My eyes glazed over a bit.

journey.quote: One couple featured in the resort's own wedding story married at the fountain and held their reception at Akasa.
journey.reaction: So you don't actually know where they do ceremonies? Feels thin for a 'best venues' list.

journey.section: Guest count, rooms and exclusive use
journey.quote: Use this table to narrow by guest numbers. Each figure is the venue's own, for the space named.
journey.reaction: This is the screenshot. Guest numbers to venue, done. Should be way higher up.

journey.section: When is the right time to get married in Bali?
journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller says weather can change quickly during the wet season, usually around October to April.
journey.reaction: Dated, so I know it's current. Good.

journey.section: How do guests get to Bali and between the areas?
journey.quote: As at November 2026, travellers arriving at Indonesia's international entry points must complete an arrival card and apply for an e-Visa on Arrival, both on the All Indonesia website.
journey.reaction: Useful, but I searched for venues, not visas. Long scroll before the FAQ.

journey.quote: Four Seasons Jimbaran Bay's Gili Jimbaran, The Mulia's Oceanfront Glass House, a COMO Uma Ubud buy-out and Mandapa's Ayung Riverside each take up to 100.
journey.reaction: Exactly the question I'd type. Short, direct answer.

journey.quote: ### Which Bali venues can host 100 guests?
journey.reaction: But no 'how much does a Bali wedding venue cost' question anywhere. Just tell me how much it costs.

journey.section: Shortlist your Bali venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: One person is nice. 'For Australian couples' though, so is this even for me in Singapore?

unanswered_questions: Roughly what does a wedding at any of these venues cost, even a starting range or a package price? (none on the page)
Why these 15 venues? Is the list chosen on anything beyond 'they host weddings'?
Do you work with couples who don't live in Australia? (deferred business detail)
How is the Wedded Concierge fee charged and roughly how much? (deferred business detail)
Can I see a real Bali wedding you've planned at one of these venues? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: | Venue | Area | Setting | Ceremony | Exclusive use |
turn_offs_found.why: The at-a-glance table is wide for a phone and its last column is 'Not published' for 13 of 15 venues, while the capacity-by-guests table I actually need sits far down the page.

turn_offs_found.quote: Use this table to narrow by guest numbers. Each figure is the venue's own, for the space named.
turn_offs_found.why: The most useful thing on the page is buried below all 15 venue write-ups; I nearly left before reaching it.

turn_offs_found.quote: Ceremony options:** Outdoors, Champa Garden, SKY, the AYANA Villa, KISIK Pier, the Asmara Gazebo from the Javanese royal palace and Bale Kencana, with its stone paths and Balinese split gate.
turn_offs_found.why: Dense lists of space names with no context are hard to scan on a phone and don't help me decide.

turn_offs_found.quote: Foreign tourists entering Bali also pay a tourist levy, separate from the visa, either online before travel or at counters at Bali's airport and seaport.
turn_offs_found.why: Visa, levy, safety and legal sections push the FAQ a long way down for someone who searched for venues.

would_share_with: My partner: a screenshot of the guest-count table and the four-area intro

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [shortlist your Bali venues through Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=bali-wedding-venues&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: Don't know the brand, no idea of cost, and it says AUD for Australian couples. Bookmark, not enquire.

top_3_changes: Move the guest-count table (or a short version) up near the Key Takeaways, or add a capacity column to the at-a-glance table and drop the mostly empty exclusive-use column on mobile.
Add a cost FAQ or a line saying plainly whether venues publish pricing, so the obvious next question isn't ignored.
Say in one line why these 15 made the list, so 'best' feels earned.
